title: Which line is parallel to line a, line b or line c?
description: Three leaning lines a, b and c are cut by a steep line. The board compares the angles the steep line makes with each, finds the angle with c matches the angle with a, and checks that c keeps the same gap from a while b closes in.
teaching_notes: One idea: lines that make the same angle with a steep line lean the same way, so they are parallel. The line that closes in is not parallel.

source: Figure it Out (parallel and perpendicular lines), Q5
video_script.why: The child knows parallel lines run the same way and now decides which of two lines is parallel to a third.
video_script.substitution: Check which line runs the same way as a, the same way as the example in the book, by comparing the angle each line makes with the steep line.
video_script.anchor: Three leaning lines a, b and c, with a steep line that meets a at one end and b and c at the other end.
video_script.payoff_line: Line c is parallel to line eigh.

final_answer.value: Line c is parallel to line a, because the angles made with the steep line are about equal, 30° and 29°
final_answer.spoken: line c is parallel to line eigh, because the angles made with the steep line are about equal, thirty degrees and twenty nine degrees

hold_back: Line c is parallel to line a, because the angles made with the steep line are about equal, 30° and 29°
maths_rules: the steep line makes about 30 degrees with a, about 29 degrees with c and about 33 degrees with b
lines that make the same angle with the steep line lean the same way
29 is close to 30, and 33 is 3 more than 30, so c is the line that matches a
parallel lines keep the same gap, and c keeps the same gap from a while b closes in
video_script.design: The three lines and the steep line stay on the stage. The angles are marked in colour and the gaps between the lines are shown at both ends.
